title: Truncated alteration descent with unchanged normal-crossing branches
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a local morphism of Noetherian strictly henselian local schemes with closed points $x',x$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Assume $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and put $U'=X'\times_XU$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix $L\geq1$. An ordinary alteration hypercover means an augmented simplicial diagram of Noetherian schemes, finite type over its base, whose maps to matching objects are covers for the Grothendieck topology generated by jointly surjective etale families and proper surjective morphisms [def-weil-pbc-topos, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A matching object is the finite limit prescribed by the faces in the lower simplicial degrees. All these limits and all pullbacks are ordinary scheme-theoretic fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an ordinary alteration hypercover given through degree $L$, and let $X'_a=X'\times_XX_a$ with its induced simplicial structure. Put $U_a=X_a\times_XU$ and $U'_a=X'_a\times_{X'}U'$, and give their closed complements reduced induced structures. Suppose for every $0\leq a\leq L$ and geometric point $z'$ of $(X'_a)_{x'}$ with image $z$ in $(X_a)_x$ that both strict localizations $(X_a)_{(z)}$ and $(X'_a)_{(z')}$ are regular; the complement of $U_a$ in the first is a strict normal crossings divisor with branch equations $f_1,\ldots,f_r$; and the pulled-back equations define the complement of $U'_a$ and have linearly independent classes in $\mathfrak m_{z'}/\mathfrak m_{z'}^2$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Empty boundaries are allowed ($r=0$). Then canonical pullback is an isomorphism
$$H^q(U,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(U',\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})\qquad(0\leq q<L),$$
for ordinary small-etale cohomology of constant abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: Expose XV, Propositions 2.1.7, 2.2.2 and 2.2.4, printed pp.221–222, truncated form N=L-1. The prime-to-ell topology is contained in the unrestricted alteration topology there; the parameter condition is 2.1.4.

proof.text:
Write $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X_a$ and $i_a:F_a\hookrightarrow X_a$ for the inclusions, and similarly with primes, where $F_a=X_a\times_Xx$, $F'_a=X'_a\times_{X'}x'$ and $p_a:F'_a\to F_a$. Ordinary Cartesian pullback gives $F'_a=F_a\times_xx'$. Put $A_a=i_a^{-1}Rj_{a,*}\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ and $A'_a=(i'_a)^{-1}Rj'_{a,*}\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$. Apply [lem-per-oriented-special-fibre-totalization] to the two augmented diagrams. Its naturality identifies canonical pullback on $H^q(U,-)$ with the totalization map whose column $a$ is
$$R\Gamma(F_a,A_a)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F'_a,p_a^{-1}A_a)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(F'_a,A'_a).$$
All schemes in these expressions are Noetherian, and every open immersion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: an open of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact and an open immersion is separated. The complexes $A_a,A'_a$ have no negative cohomology, since they are inverse images of the right derived functor applied to a degree-zero sheaf.

source.place: XV Proposition 2.2.2 and proof of 2.2.4; XII Theorem 2.2.4

proof.text: Fix $a\leq L$ and a geometric point $z'$ of $F'_a$, with image $z$. The stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] for the qcqs open immersions identifies the exchange on cohomology stalks with pullback from the open in $(X_a)_{(z)}$ to the corresponding open in $(X'_a)_{(z')}$. These strict localizations are Noetherian strictly henselian and regular by the hypotheses; write $R$ for the local ring of $(X_a)_{(z)}$, $R'$ for that of $(X'_a)_{(z')}$, and $R\to R'$ for the local homomorphism. The branch equations $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ lie in $\mathfrak m_R$, since every nonempty closed subset of a local scheme contains its closed point. They have independent classes in $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2$: by [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] for the full index set, $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is regular of dimension $\dim R-r$, so its maximal ideal needs exactly $\dim R-r$ generators, i.e. $\dim\mathfrak m_R/(\mathfrak m_R^2+(f_1,\ldots,f_r))=\dim R-r$, and the $r$ classes of the $f_i$ span an $r$-dimensional subspace of $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2$ (for $r=0$ there is nothing to check). The pulled-back equations have independent classes in $\mathfrak m_{R'}/\mathfrak m_{R'}^2$ by the explicit assumption, and $V(\prod_if_i)$ pulls back to the complement of $U'_a$ there. Apply [lem-per-strict-local-snc-kummer-cohomology] to these local rings. Choose in $R$ a root of unity $\zeta$ whose existence that statement supplies, and use its image in $R'$ for the target identification. The image still satisfies $\zeta^\ell=1$ and $1-\zeta^b\in R'^\times$ for $1\leq b<\ell$, since a ring map preserves units. Pullback sends the Kummer cup-product basis indexed by increasing $q$-subsets of the $r$ branches to the basis with the same indices. Thus the stalk exchange is an isomorphism in every degree, also for $q=0$ and $r=0$. Negative cohomology vanishes on both sides. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative], $p_a^{-1}A_a\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_a$.

source.place: XV Proposition 2.1.7, proof by branch generators; Definition 2.1.4

proof.text: The residue fields $k=\kappa(x)$ and $k'=\kappa(x')$ are separably closed, and $\ell$ is invertible in them. The scheme $F_a$ is finite type over $k$, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-kun-0f1c] to $F_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the extension $k'/k$, and the bounded-below complex $A_a$, whose cohomology is killed by $\ell$. It identifies $R(F'_a\to x')_*p_a^{-1}A_a$ with the pullback of $R(F_a\to x)_*A_a$. On a separably closed field, global sections evaluate a sheaf at the terminal point and are exact, by [lem-kun-0ezp]: every etale object is a disjoint union of copies of that point. Pullback between two such points preserves this value (a constant group stays the same constant group). Consequently the first arrow in Step 1 is an isomorphism. Step 2 proves that its second arrow is an isomorphism for every $a\leq L$, so the column comparison is a quasi-isomorphism in each specified degree.

source.place: XV proof of Proposition 2.2.4, invariance under extension of separably closed residue fields; Stacks Tag 0F1C, etale-cohomology-lemma-base-change-field-extension

proof.text: Use the nonnegative double-complex models of [lem-per-oriented-special-fibre-totalization] and total degrees as in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Quotient each model by its subcomplex of columns $a>L$; the discarded subcomplex has no terms below total degree $L+1$, so the quotient induces the same cohomology in degrees $q<L$. The comparison of the two quotients is a quasi-isomorphism: filter its mapping cone by the finitely many columns $0,\ldots,L$. Each successive quotient is the cone of a column comparison, shifted by that column index, and is acyclic by Steps 2–3. The long exact cohomology sequences for these finite successive extensions show, inductively, that the whole cone is acyclic. Thus the truncated totalizations have isomorphic $H^q$ for $q<L$. This also proves directly that no unprescribed higher column can affect the answer: to test cycles and boundaries in degree $q$ one uses total degrees $q-1,q,q+1$, all at most $L$. The naturality in Step 1 identifies this isomorphism with the required canonical pullback.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q49-8a5fab7f1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, the statements of all cited nodes, and the sources: ILO XV 2.1.1–2.2.5 (pp. 220–222), XII 2.1.1–2.3.2 (pp. 191–193), II 2.3, the alt/T recap at the start of III §3, and XVI Cor. 3.1.3 (pp. 242–243). E7 statement change accepted: the base item's alt/X version, with dominant-reduced matching objects and pullbacks, is false. I checked the worker's counterexample independently: X=Spec k[[x,y]], U=D(xy), Y=Bl₀X, X'=Spec k[[t]] with x,y↦t. The dominant pullback of constant Y is the identity hypercover of X'. At the slope-1 point the only branch is x, which pulls back to t, so every hypothesis holds, but H¹(U)=F_ℓ² while H¹(U')=F_ℓ (L=2). The corrected version uses ordinary products and étale/proper-surjective covers, as in XII 2.1.1/2.2.4 and XV 2.2.3. The coefficient, the hypotheses for a≤L and the conclusion for q<L (N=L−1) are unchanged, so it is not easier than the source. Steps 1, 3 and 4 check out: F'_a=F_a×_x x'; 0f1c applies to F_a→Spec k with ℓ invertible, and 0ezp to the separably closed points; the finite column filtration of the cone is a genuine few-line argument. New nodes are true and not duplicates. lem-per-oriented-special-fibre-totalization is XII 2.2.4(i) / XV 2.2.2 with naturality and the truncated form; tested on the identity hypercover and V=∅; it assumes no regularity, so it does not restate the item. lem-per-strict-local-snc-kummer-cohomology is XV 2.1.2 / XVI 3.1.3 at a strictly local point; tested r=0, r=1, q>r, ℓ=2. The nearest existing node, lem-per-regular-normal-crossings-constant-image, gives only constructibility and vanishing. No SGA is cited and there is no cycle. The declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. FIX (2 small faults, both in Step 2; file in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/): (a) the ζ choice had the direction of R→R' reversed; now ζ is chosen in R and its image used in R'; (b) source-side cotangent independence was not justified; I wrote the two-line argument from def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary (R/(f) regular of dimension dim R−r) and added that node to Step 2 uses and proof_deps.
